title: Run Calibration on the shared worker with recovery

verify.summary: Independent disposable PostgreSQL evidence disproved durable live-run interruption: a crash during sequential evaluation rolls the run back to requested and permits automatic rerun, violating FT-011-AC-005.

Attempt 3 independently reproduced the disposable live evaluator crash after a durable running claim: startup records interrupted and idle, queued Photo resumes, no Calibration reruns automatically, and only a fresh explicit request completes. Sequential direct binding, fail-closed asset handling, unchanged serving/startup binding and excluded infrastructure were also observed.

Attempt 4 independently ran an isolated crash exactly after the durable running claim and before worker operation/evaluation: recovery records interrupted and idle, queued Photo resumes, no Calibration auto-runs, and only an explicit new request completes. The same probe proves sequential direct SFace-release-Buffalo M binding, direct-adapter cv2.error terminal failure, and unchanged serving/startup binding.

Attempt 4 semantic verification reproduced a real S3 NoSuchKey path that leaves the selected Calibration run running after worker release instead of recording the required terminal dataset_unavailable failure.

evidence_required: FT-011-AC-005 RED (to obtain before production change; none is backfilled for this historical in_progress task): an isolated requested Calibration run cannot complete the selected direct SFace -> release -> Buffalo M binding while preserving the committed serving revision and normal startup adapter binding; GREEN: only while current_operation=calibration, the existing singleton worker binds the selected eligible SFace adapter, releases it, then binds the selected eligible Buffalo M adapter from configured read-only assets, and records missing or identity/checksum-mismatched assets as a failed run before releasing for Photo work; decisive comparison: the same disposable scenario snapshots serving revision and normal startup binding before/after, records binding order/release and terminal run/worker/Photo state, and proves no simultaneous preload, registry, second worker or automatic replacement/retry; artifact: focused worker-test output and runtime trace under .tasks/TASK-101-T3-FT-011-W2/.
purpose: Connect durable Calibration runs to the already accepted singleton worker and recovery lifecycle without adding scheduling machinery.
success_outcome: A developer-requested run executes only while the shared worker is idle; restart leaves it visibly interrupted, resumes ordinary Photo processing and requires an explicit new request to rerun.
anti_goals: Do not add a second worker, preemption, priority, generic scheduler/queue, automatic retry or replacement run.
Do not change Photo claim/failure semantics or the existing single-slot CPU policy.
Do not implement recommendation algorithms, staff HTTP, apply, promotion or retention.

forbidden_scope: Production worker/processes, operator/default queues and non-disposable Calibration/Photo rows
New worker services, scheduler state, priority/preemption and automatic Calibration rerun
Photo processing algorithm/publication behavior and serving configuration
stop_conditions: Correct execution cannot reuse BackgroundPhotoWorker and its existing calibration operation without a new scheduler or worker.
Startup recovery cannot make stale running terminal and restore ordinary Photo work without changing accepted Photo recovery semantics.
The runtime probe cannot use isolated disposable state, deterministic restart, safe rerun and complete cleanup.

constraints: Reuse BackgroundPhotoWorker, WorkerClaimRepository and the existing current_operation=calibration state; diagnostics owns run transitions and processing owns worker state.
Claim one requested run only when idle, release the worker after every terminal path and never create a replacement run during recovery.
Use a known isolated run and queued Photo with a deterministic restart, safe rerun and complete cleanup.
invariants: At most one background operation occupies the singleton worker and Calibration may delay but never preempt Photo work.
Worker restart never fabricates a complete result or automatic rerun.
Photo processing resumes under its existing claim/recovery rules after Calibration becomes terminal.
TASK-101 retains the original FT-011-AC-005 ownership only as immutable historical failed evidence; it has no active executable claim or dependent-promotion role.
verification_targets: Focused disposable worker fixture proves selected SFace -> release -> Buffalo M direct binding from configured read-only assets only during current_operation=calibration, with the committed serving revision and normal startup adapter binding unchanged before and after.

The same fixture proves a missing or identity/checksum-mismatched selected asset fails that Calibration run, releases the worker, preserves serving/startup binding and allows queued Photo work to resume.

Restart during a running selected-binding scenario proves interrupted, idle restoration, queued Photo progress and zero automatically created replacement runs; focused source/fixture inspection proves reuse of one existing worker/direct adapters with no simultaneous preload, registry, second worker or automatic retry.
